headline: Complex Surgery Successfully Separates Fijian Conjoined Twins
meta_description: Doctors in Saudi Arabia successfully separated 13-month-old Fijian conjoined twins Dicecea and Jesepeli Kikau after a rare and complex operation.
summary_short: In an exceptionally rare procedure, surgeons in Saudi Arabia have successfully separated two Fijian sisters who were born joined at the lower abdomen and pelvis.
body:
Doctors in Saudi Arabia have successfully completed a complex operation to separate 13-month-old conjoined twins Dicecea and Jesepeli Kikau from Fiji. The sisters were born with omphalo-ischiopagus tetrapus, an exceptionally rare condition in which they were joined at the lower abdomen and pelvis.

The nearly 13-hour operation required surgeons to carefully separate the girls' shared liver, bowel, and urinary tract. Despite their connection, each sister had her own heart and lungs, which significantly affected the surgical approach and gave them better prospects for survival.

This successful separation represents a major medical achievement for a condition so uncommon that most surgeons never encounter it in their careers. Both girls now have the chance to grow and develop as separate individuals.
quick_facts: 13-month-old Fijian twins Dicecea and Jesepeli Kikau successfully separated
Surgery performed in Saudi Arabia lasted nearly 13 hours
Exceptionally rare condition: omphalo-ischiopagus tetrapus joining lower abdomen and pelvis
Each sister had her own heart and lungs before separation
